titel: #127 - Beating The Angel of Death: How He Survived Being Shot Point Blank by A Child Predator w/Ali Perez

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Surviving a point-blank rifle shot by a child predator and a profound near-death…
kurzfassung: Ali Perez recounts his demanding career as a Navy diver, his transition into San Diego law enforcement, and his response to the 2001 Santana High School shooting. He details the harrowing day in 2012 when he was shot twice with a .308 rifle while serving a warrant on a child predator. During the ensuing gunfight and close-quarters ordeal, he experienced a profound spiritual vision that forever changed his life.
stichpunkte: Growing up in Austin, Texas, and finding inspiration to join the Navy after seeing a documentary on diving.
Serving as a Navy diver in Coronado and Pearl Harbor, conducting submarine maintenance and hazardous recovery operations.
Transitioning to the San Diego County Sheriff's Department and working extensive shifts in the county jail system.
Responding to the Santana High School shooting in 2001 and confronting the teenage gunman.
Promoting to the child abuse detective unit to investigate crimes against vulnerable children.
Executing a warrant on September 25, 2012, where he was ambushed and shot point-blank twice with an M1 Garand .308 rifle.
Enduring an 11-minute firefight and near-fatal blood loss while trapped inside the suspect's apartment.
Experiencing a powerful, transformative vision of Jesus Christ and the spiritual realm while dying.
Undergoing dozens of surgeries and a miraculous medical recovery against the odds.
Writing a new chapter of faith, forgiveness, and sharing his story of survival and divine grace.

kapitel.titel: Early Life and Navy Diving Career
Transition to Law Enforcement and Jail Operations

clips.hook: Wrestling underwater at nearly 200 feet deep due to nitrogen narcosis.
clips.text: The guest explains how deep-sea nitrogen absorption caused him and his partner to experience severe intoxication effects, leading them to playfully tackle each other on the ocean floor during a qualification dive.

clips.hook: A terrifying training entrapment inside the ballast tank of a submarine.
clips.text: A fellow diver became tightly wedged inside the narrow internal machinery of a submarine under extreme heat, requiring a full-scale rescue operation that served as a stark reminder of industrial underwater dangers.

clips.hook: Confronting a 15-year-old active school shooter in a smoke-filled restroom.
clips.text: Officers breached a school bathroom during a shooting incident and faced a young teenager holding a revolver with its cylinder open, forcing an immediate life-or-death tactical decision.

clips.hook: Standing over a fatally wounded officer, the assailant asks a bizarre question.
clips.text: After shooting the detective multiple times and causing catastrophic injuries, the suspect casually walked over, kicked away a magazine, and calmly asked where the service weapon was kept.

clips.hook: Surgeons prepare organ donation paperwork while his family is told he won't surv
clips.text: Medical staff informed the family that the patient's massive blood loss was unsurvivable, prompting them to initiate preparations for organ donation while hundreds of fellow officers gathered in support.

beschreibung:
Former Navy diver and San Diego County law enforcement veteran Ali Perez survived an encounter that should have ended his life. What began as an operation to arrest a suspected child predator turned into a close-range gunfight after Ali entered a darkened apartment and was met by a rifle.
Watch the episode here: https://youtu.be/8MHOYdFxiIw
Ali describes being shot multiple times, suffering catastrophic injuries, becoming trapped inside the apartment with the gunman, continuing to fight while severely wounded, running out of ammunition, and eventually believing he was about to die.
Then the story takes a turn that Ali says changed the rest of his life.
This conversation goes far beyond that single day.
Ali takes us inside Navy dive school, including the brutal underwater training and what happens to the human mind nearly 200 feet beneath the surface. He recounts responding to a school shooting and helping apprehend the teenage shooter, the psychological aftermath of seeing children killed, his thoughts on law enforcement response during active-shooter incidents, and the disturbing reality of investigating physical and sexual crimes against children.
He also walks us through the aftermath of his own shooting: massive blood loss, emergency surgery, his family being warned that he likely would not survive, years of recovery, 43 surgeries, faith, forgiveness and rebuilding a life after everything changes in seconds.
Whether you share Ali's beliefs or question what he experienced, this is a conversation about what happens when a man reaches the absolute edge of life and has to decide what comes next.
